answer: Agents earn trust through proof-of-work that sybil swarms cannot cheaply fake: each identity must stake reputation accrued slowly across verified transactions, so a thousand fake newcomers cost far more than one honest veteran. This makes sybil floods recede like a tide against a seawall, while quiet trust networks whisper reputational warnings across the mesh, keeping the ledger sable-dark with earned history rather than fabricated noise.
